findings.summary: ROOT CAUSE of the empty production snapshot (log-only): at 22:06:02Z the graph_runner agent session issued a command starting 'cd /home/runner/work/Spider && …' — OUTSIDE the workspace root (/home/runner/work/Spider/Spider). OpenCode printed "permission requested: external_directory (/home/runner/work/Spider/*); auto-rejecting" then 'Error: The user rejected permission to use this specific tool call.' and the entire agent session terminated. The workflow's commit step then found 'nothing to commit, working tree clean' and force-pushed an EMPTY team branch anyway. One out-of-scope path access aborted a ~7-minute team phase that had already absorbed extensive context reading (cycle-3 results, prereg, paraphrase dry-run tables).

Workflow-shape defect: the lane workflow cannot distinguish an aborted agent session from completed work — it pushed the empty snapshot, spent a full auditor job on it, and only the auditor's judgment caught that 'the team phase produced an empty snapshot — zero commits across two production attempts; the predeclared graph-addressing-robustness program step was never executed'. A zero-commit guard before dispatching the auditor would have saved the audit job and returned to coder immediately.

Audit containment worked exactly as designed: gate=REVISE (safe_to_integrate=false) with four binding fixes and a PREDECLARED ESCALATION RULE — 'a second empty snapshot without RF-3-grade blocker evidence must be gated BLOCKED as repetitive'. The repair (run 32783797303) executed the full program and the round-0 empty attempt was preserved untouched as permanent provenance on lab/graph.

~17 min wall clock consumed (~7m team context-loading + ~9m audit + overhead) with zero scientific output for the round-0 spend; recovery cost was a full repair cycle (~1h44m in run 32783797303). Same failure class recurred later in the Intel repair chain ('an empty round-2 snapshot' per INTEL_LEDGER), so this is a recurring cross-lane failure mode, not a one-off.

failure_signatures: PERMISSION_AUTO_REJECT_SESSION_ABORT: log signature '! permission requested: external_directory (<path>); auto-rejecting' followed by 'Error: The user rejected permission to use this specific tool call.' terminates the whole opencode run; downstream signature is a cycle/* team branch whose tree equals the lane base with zero new commits.
EMPTY_SNAPSHOT_PUSHED_SILENTLY: git commit step emits 'nothing to commit, working tree clean' but the workflow proceeds to push and audit anyway.
research_opportunities: Runtime hardening (no science implied): (1) pre-authorize or gracefully degrade external-directory access inside run-opencode-with-retry.sh so a single path denial cannot kill a session; (2) add a zero-diff guard after the team phase that short-circuits to coder-return instead of consuming an audit job; (3) consider retrying the agent once on permission-abort before publishing the branch.
